item.title: US criticises Ukraine's 'deep strike' campaign against Russia
item.description: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called the US' warning "quite a stupid thing," while his British counterpart Wes Streeting said there was "no doubt" in his mind that Ukraine's long-range strikes had "helped to degrade Putin's war machine."

item.title: Five viral moments from Pope Leo XIV's South American tour
item.description: Pope Leo XIV's South American tour brought several memorable moments, from an unexpected encounter with a flying rosary bracelet to a helicopter journey into Peru's remote Andes.

item.title: GTA 6: What to know about the upcoming Grand Theft Auto game
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI is generating huge excitement across Asia, despite restrictions on sales, censorship and the dominance of mobile gaming. While the game is not officially licensed in mainland China and faces content restrictions in Japan, fans are finding ways to access the franchise.

item.title: Dead Melbourne Cup racehorse found dumped in Sydney waste facility
item.description: REC Equine Specialists said So You Are had been euthanised before being collected by a "contracted provider" and taken to a "licensed landfill." The practice has apologised and said the horse should have been "promptly and respectfully buried."

item.title: US strikes targets in Qeshm Island after Iranian mines hit five ships in Hormuz
item.description: Iran says the US military carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island in southern Iran, while at least five ships were set on fire by mines in the Strait of Hormuz earlier in the day.

item.title: Russia cannot have a say over NATO's military activities, Norwegian foreign minister warns
item.description: Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide told Euronews that Moscow must not be allowed to dictate Europe's security arrangements while also warning against a return to spheres of influence.

item.title: French foreign minister slams Lavrov accusations about 'direct participation' in Ukraine war
item.description: Russia said on Tuesday it was aware of French troops deployed to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in the war and saying a message had been issued to Paris. France has rejected the claim troops are directly involved in fighting as "absurd."

item.title: EU climate chief Hoekstra: Electrification key for Europe to compete with China as COP pushes global target
item.description: Hoekstra tells On the Record that electrification is key to Europe's industrial competitiveness, as COP talks push for a global target of 35% by 2035.

item.title: EU economy chief Dombrovskis warns France to rein in debt as growth outlook improves
item.description: EU economy chief Dombrovskis warns France to rein in debt as growth outlook improves

item.title: New anti-regime protests erupt in flashpoint Iranian city
item.description: A protest sparked by a deadly bus crash in a western Iranian city turned into a new anti-regime protest with hundreds chanting "Death to the dictator."

item.title: Moldova closes airspace after 'Shahed-type' drone detected heading towards Chișinău
item.description: "Russia's war threatens all of Europe," President Maia Sandu wrote in a post on social media, adding that "several Russian drones" had violated Moldovan airspace on Tuesday.

item.title: 19 people rescued after gas carrier 'struck' in Black Sea
item.description: It marks the latest in a string of similar incidents in the Black Sea believed to be linked to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Euronews Verify: What's at stake as Europe seeks to triple its data centre capacity?
item.description: Europe wants to triple its data centre capacity, but residents and environmental campaigners are taking to the streets to demand a pause on new data centre projects. Why? And what’s at stake?

item.title: Beyond the green premium: Competitive advantage through decarbonization
item.description: 'The opportunities that decarbonization offers have never been greater', explains Noam Boussidan, Head of the First Movers Coalition, in an op-ed for Euronews. In stable conditions, fossil-based inputs may look cheaper, but that advantage is quickly lost when supply is disrupted or prices spike.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Eurozone growth forecast at 1.2%, Ukraine strikes Crimea bridge
item.description: The EU forecasts 1.2% Eurozone growth amid inflation and debt concerns, analysed live tonight by Valdis Dombrovskis. Meanwhile, Ukraine strikes a key Russia-Crimea bridge ahead of talks with Norway's Foreign Minister, and Spain's Pedro Sánchez slams EU Rwanda asylum plans.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 17th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 17th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: North Macedonia prevents 'terrorist' assassination plot targeting person in Greece
item.description: Guns and sketches marking specific locations were reportedly seized as part of the operation, which was carried out in cooperation with Greece's national intelligence agency.

item.title: Jensen Huang breaks silence says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia's CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang says he’s open to returning in his first statement since resignation.

item.title: Hormone-disrupting chemicals pose growing health threat, UN warns
item.description: Hormone-disrupting chemicals found in everyday products pose growing risks to human health and the environment, while regulations remain insufficient to tackle them, warns the UN.

item.title: Brazilian chicken ban: EU delays decision despite positive audit
item.description: Mercosur meat imports remain a contentious issue among EU countries, amid divisions over a deal liberalising trade between the two blocs.

item.title: Trump warns Iran over allegations of dirty bomb threat to Washington
item.description: Iran denied media reports based on US intelligence that it may be planning a dirty bomb attack in the US capital, with questions swirling about its actual intentions or real capabilities for such an act, but Trump issued a strong warning against Tehran "because they happen to be crazy."

item.title: ‘Change is possible’: Danish offshore wind giant wins Earthshot Prize after quitting oil and gas
item.description: Inspired by John F. Kennedy’s Moonshot, which united millions around the goal of reaching the moon, Prince William’s Earthshot Prize is one of the world’s most prestigious environmental awards.

item.title: Apple to face landmark trial in France over alleged planned obsolescence of iPhones
item.description: If found guilty, the US tech firm could face fines of up to 5% of its annual revenue, equal to roughly €21.7 billion.

item.title: Jensen Huang to face US Congress interviews on Nvidia’s sales to China on 1 December
item.description: Huang is set to appear before the United States' House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee on 1 December.

item.title: UK urged to overhaul youth benefits as one million young people drift out of work and study
item.description: The review’s author says only Romania fares worse in Europe on youth inactivity, even though young Britons are less likely to be unemployed than their peers in France, Spain or Italy.

item.title: 46 people injured after two trains collide in Prague
item.description: Ivan Bednárik, the Czech Republic's minister for transport, thanked paramedics and firefighters for their "professional and swift response" and said authorities had launched an investigation into the incident.

item.title: Why gold and silver prices have fallen to their lowest in over a year
item.description: Gold and silver prices have slumped to their lowest levels in more than a year as a strong US dollar, high bond yields and bets on another US interest rate hike sap demand. The gold price is on track for its biggest annual fall since 2015.

item.title: Russia plays for time as Europe and US push for direct peace talks
item.description: The next phase of the peace talks remains uncertain as Russia continues to play down the possibility of face-to-face talks with Europe, despite mounting pressure from Washington to make it happen.

item.title: Watch: today’s top No Comment videos from around the world
item.description: A robot pianist takes on a human musician in Italy, Pope Leo XIV has an unexpected encounter in Peru, and snow transforms the English countryside. Meanwhile, gamers compete for the European Tetris title in Denmark, while Kim Jong Un showcases North Korea's latest ski resort.

item.title: Egypt pitches reforms and energy plans at World Economic Forum meeting
item.description: At a World Economic Forum meeting in Cairo, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi pledged to simplify business procedures and outlined plans for industry, energy and AI. The government is preparing a 2027–2030 economic programme to boost productivity and give private businesses a larger role.

item.title: Computer love or hate: Charlotte de Witte's AI singer collaboration divides techno fans
item.description: The international DJ released the EP Azadi with NAVA, a virtual AI singer, to represent Iranian women banned from performing publicly, but techno star's choice has not gone down well with some of her fans.

item.title: EU’s Rwanda migrant return plan faces backlash over human rights concerns rights record
item.description: Kigali’s human rights record is under scrutiny as it prepares to host the first EU return hubs outside the bloc. Rwanda’s Interior Minister rejected the criticism, pointing out to the country's experience in dealing with migrants.

item.title: My favourite things: Netflix's content chief Larry Tanz shares his best-of watchlist
item.description: Netflix's EMEA content chief Larry Tanz is not one of those people who believes in having too much choice. On the sidelines of The Big Question, he spoke to Euronews Culture about how he picks what to watch, his favourite film and documentary, plus what he's looking forward to most in 2027.

item.title: Serbian MiG-29 fighter jet crashes near Belgrade, killing pilot
item.description: Developed by the Soviet Union's Mikoyan-Gurevich Design Bureau in the early 1970s, the MiG-29 entered service with the Soviet military in 1983.

item.title: 'Human rights situation is dire': MEP Tineke Strik condemns five EU nations' Rwanda return hub plan
item.description: "If you take the country of Rwanda, the human rights situation is dire" MEP Tineke Strik on Europe Tonight as five EU countries have announced they are planning to set up migrant return hubs in Rwanda.

item.title: Robots and river breezes: how China is greening its cities
item.description: From a Shenzhen lab designing buildings to be taken apart and reused to a Guangzhou skyscraper cooled by river breezes, China is testing how to cut carbon from the buildings that drive city emissions, as it works towards net zero by 2060.

item.title: Uzbekistan’s mountain lakes and trails draw visitors in every season
item.description: Emerald lakes, mountain trails and boat trips offer different ways to experience the Tashkent region, where seasonal landscapes and growing tourism are bringing more visitors into the mountains.

item.title: Deutsche Bank shares fall as leak reveals Trump tax document error
item.description: Deutsche Bank shares fell more than 6% on Tuesday after reports based on 15 million leaked records shed light on its dealings with clients including Donald Trump.

item.title: High tobacco use among European women and girls is ‘worrying,’ WHO warns
item.description: Women’s tobacco use is falling at a much slower rate than men’s, according to WHO Europe.

item.title: EU's 2040 climate target at risk as bloc waters down carbon market reform
item.description: A leaked compromise proposal seeks to shield European industry from rising carbon costs, but environmental groups warn that concessions on free emissions allowances and international carbon credits could undermine the bloc's 2040 climate ambitions.

item.title: Fresh public sector strike in France under way over pay as government struggles to pass budget
item.description: Tuesday's demonstrations follow talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, which left unions dissatisfied, as they continue to push for across the board pay rises.

item.title: 'Absurd': France rejects claim its troops are directly participating in Ukraine war
item.description: Russia said on Tuesday it was aware of French troops deployed to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in the war and saying a message had been issued to Paris. France has rejected the claim troops are directly involved in fighting as "absurd."

item.title: Drivers battle blizzard conditions in England’s Yorkshire Dales
item.description: Early snow brings blizzard conditions to northern England, with drivers navigating treacherous roads and poor visibility across the Yorkshire Dales.

item.title: Finland’s satellite provider Iceye bids €2 billion for Italian rocket maker Avio
item.description: The satellite firm is promising €1 billion of investment in Italy, but the deal is likely to face scrutiny in Rome, which has a say through its stake in Avio’s biggest shareholder.

item.title: Qatar warns Gulf escalation poses 'grave danger' and announces new talks with Iran
item.description: Qatar warns the US and Iran to "avoid any escalation" as Iran's new attacks in Bahrain and its strikes on Gulf shipping are putting diplomacy under pressure. Qatar's foreign ministry announces new talks with Tehran, aiming to bridge the divide between US and Iran.

item.title: Moment Ukrainian drones strike the Kerch Bridge linking Crimea to Russia
item.description: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to annexed Crimea for a second consecutive night, forcing its closure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the operation as unprecedented, saying it had been prepared over several weeks.

item.title: Basel, Baia Mare and Omiš named Europe’s Christmas capitals for 2027
item.description: Basel in Switzerland, Baia Mare in Romania and Omiš in Croatia have been recognised as 2027’s Christmas capital, city and village, respectively.

item.title: Second tanker in two days sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, search operation under way
item.description: The tanker had disappeared from radar shortly after midnight, and by 8:02 am (07:02 CET) local time the emergency buoy was activated, emitting a signal for a sunken ship.

item.title: EU preliminarily finds Temu broke rules on illegal and unsafe products
item.description: The preliminary findings point to weak product checks, content moderation and seller sanctions, potentially exposing the Chinese online marketplace to a fine of up to 6% of its global annual turnover.

item.title: EU readies fresh sanctions on Russia amid 'absurd' demands and winter strikes
item.description: A new round of EU sanctions against Russia is already in the works. Banks, crypto platforms and the "shadow fleet" are the likeliest targets.
